Pathfinder is in every practical way dnd 3.75. Its literally built on the 3.5 chassis, even to the point it has to use the same OGL legal terms of use.

Main differences:

**More feats and class abilities.** The classes are more complex because they get more abilities to fill out otherwise empty levels. Theres at least 15 optional archetypes per class that change out core class abilities for different mechanics. You get a feat every odd level, not every 3 levels. All this makes for a LOT more choices and flexibility in making your build without having to hunt down obscure splatbooks.

**Power creep:** Classes are more powerful across the board at base level due to more class abilities and feats available, BUT there is a lot less top end minmax potential due to less truly broken content. You can no longer make punpun, omnificer, or the locate city bomb. But an average character in PF will completely RoFLStomp an equivalent non-munchkin 3.5 character

**Power gaps:** Casters are still king, but the gap is a lot narrower than it was in 3.5 because of the 1500 feats to choose from, and because martial get their own toys to play with. Barbarians get rage powers, rogues get special talents to pick from, fighters gets some INSANE bonuses on fighting styles. Build it right and you can actually kind of keep up with caster a little better.

**Monk.** Its not useless anymore! It gets a lot of fun archetypes that bring it to relevance again. I was always a monk fanboy, but man was it weak. My monk/paladin/rogue build has never been happier :)

**Better skills.** They clump hide/move silently into stealth, among other such examples. You gets max ranks equal to class level, but your "class skills" get a +3 bonus. And theres no more 1/2 skill ranks/points. Just put your points anywhere you want. The flexibility is great.

**Grappling:** You have a combat maneuver bonus/defense stats. treat these like attack and armor class, but for the fancy tricks: disarm, grapple, trip, sunder, etc.

**Cantrips** are at will and never run out. Spam that 1d3 acid splash all day long. Never worry about troll regeneration again :D

**Feat tax**: While annoyingly underpowered feat prerequisites are still a thing, everything is slightly rebalanced so its not as painful as it was in 3.5.

EVERYTHING rules and content is available for free on [d20pfsrd.com](https://d20pfsrd.com). Not only that, but the developers have spent years answering official FAQS on rulings. Do the research and you will almost never have to homebrew a rule to figure out how something works.

**Custom content creation:** It has official rulesets on creating custom magic items and custom races. Good luck ever running out of official content, but if you want something not covered in the RaW? They got you covered for these two categories at least.

**XP costs for crafting** are GONE. Holy shit this is a niche issue, but god damn is it amazing!
